reason: C2 is the most specific and well-defined hypothesis. It proposes a concrete intervention (high-energy particle irradiation) and provides a clear mechanism (scattering of phonons by point defects) that is specific to the HfNbTaTiZr system. The predicted outcome (reduced phonon thermal conductivity) is quantified, and the hypothesis includes a decisive falsification test (measuring thermal conductivity of irradiated and unirradiated samples). Additionally, C2 acknowledges the limitation of the available measurements (1 wt.% oxygen) and specifies the material state (polycrystalline) and temperature range (300-1200 K) for which the prediction applies. While other candidates also propose plausible interventions, they lack the specificity and detail of C2.
